text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Heads may roll at the Ministry of Education headquarters following a one-week ultimatum President Bakili Muluzi issued on Thursday to senior officials after he was angered by civil servants' attitudes and slow work in government and unpaid teachers.

- The Blantyre High Court on Thursday granted an injunction to withhold results of university entrance examinations scheduled to be released in May, following an application by a student who wants them nullified.

- Malawi police intend to seek help from Interpol after an alleged Dubai drug tycoon's consignment of 200,000 tablets of mandrax, which was seized at Lilongwe International Airport two weeks ago, slipped out of the country.

- Five heavily armed gangsters brandishing AK47 rifles got away with more than K80,000 ($5,300) cash after bringing Blantyre's main highway under a 30 minute siege as they invaded an industrial concern.
- President Muluzi confirmed on Thursday some unscrupulous businessmen in the country were defrauding individuals and companies under the guise of multiplying money through "juju".

- A proposal by the opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) to gain more power by a merger with the Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) opposition was thrown out at the weekend when the two parties met in Lilongwe, the administrative capital.
- A hospital employee in Mzimba, northern Malawi, Emmanuel Nkosi, was on Thursday sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment for defiling a 3-year-old child.
